name: Brunei
summary_text: Brunei's Sharia Penal Code contains one of the world's most explicit trans-specific criminal provisions: Section 198 creates an offence of "a man posing as a woman or vice versa", and the Bruneian government has confirmed in its official guidance that the code applies to all persons in the country including tourists — travel agents are briefed accordingly. A separate indecency provision criminalises clothing that "tarnishes the image of Islam" with fines and imprisonment, and same-sex intimacy carries a stoning sentence (under a formal moratorium since 2019, with whipping and long prison terms actively available). Enforcement is quiet rather than predatory — no prosecution of a foreign visitor under these provisions has been documented — but the country is an absolute monarchy with heavy surveillance, censorship, and no LGBT organising of any kind, and LGBT Bruneians have fled abroad. The legal exposure for a discovered trans visitor is categorical: no recognition, no protection, and gender expression itself is a written offence.

sources.title: Brunei implements stoning to death under anti-LGBT laws
sources.claim_summary: BBC (April 2019): Brunei implemented strict new Islamic penal provisions making anal sex and adultery punishable by stoning to death, theft by amputation; homosexuality was already illegal (up to 10 years). Brunei's gay community expressed shock and fear; the Sultan called for 'stronger' Islamic teachings. No execution has been carried out since 1957; the law mostly applies to Muslims.

AP (Apr 2019): 'Brunei death penalty moratorium applied to new Shariah laws' — the sultan says the capital-punishment moratorium covers the new Shariah penal code allowing stoning for gay sex and adultery; under the prior law homosexuality was already punishable by up to 10 years.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying France24 piece (April 2019) covers the fear gripping Brunei's gay community after the Sharia penal code came into force.

sources.title: Here's What It's Like to Be Gay in Brunei
sources.claim_summary: TIME (April 2019): first-person reporting on what it is like to be gay in Brunei after homosexuality became punishable by stoning to death under the new Sharia penal code; describes the climate of fear in the small sultanate.

UK House of Commons Library debate pack (April 2019) on LGBT rights in Brunei: the Syariah Penal Code Order 2013 (in force in stages, final stage 3 April 2019) requires death by stoning for extramarital sex, anal sex and abortion; 40 lashes for lesbian sex; amputation for theft. HRW called it 'barbaric'; the UN High Commissioner urged Brunei to halt it.

sources.title: Maps of anti-LGBT Laws Country by Country | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW '#OUTLAWED' global map feature: at least 67 countries criminalise same-sex relations and at least nine criminalise forms of gender expression. Notes that among countries expressly forbidding trans expression, Brunei and Oman have national laws criminalising 'posing as' or 'imitating' a person of a different sex.

sources.title: Brunei - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2017 Human Rights Report for Brunei: official assessment covering the Sharia Penal Code's provisions (including death by stoning for anal sex/adultery, 40 lashes for lesbian sex), enforcement practices, and societal treatment - the report covers the period after international condemnation led Brunei to announce a moratorium on the death penalty for the code.
